packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export: Extension points and data types for exporting a structure view to a file: a provider picks a renderer for each column of the view, and the renderer fills header and data cells through format-neutral cell and column interfaces. The plugin drives the export; other plugins contribute renderers.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.e: Excel-specific refinements of the export cell and column interfaces, used when the export format is `ExportFormat.MS_EXCEL`. Renderers that know they write to a spreadsheet can cast to these to set styles, indentation and rich text.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.p: Printable (HTML page) refinements of the export cell and column interfaces, used when the export format is `ExportFormat.PRINTABLE`. They let a renderer emit raw HTML, add CSS classes and choose how percentages and durations look.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio: Internal extension points through which companion apps plug into the core plugin: contributing widget configuration and REST data, describing their licence for support reports, and declaring which structures they are integrated with. Not meant for general third-party use.

The licence data model shared by the plugin and its companion apps: licence details, licence types, hosting kinds, sources and error codes. Under the replacement's no-Marketplace ruling (SPEC 1.1) every licence the plugin reports is treated as licensed, valid and not expiring.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder: Folders: named, storable items that can be placed in a structure to group rows. The package holds the immutable folder value and the manager component that stores folders.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest: Access to forests (ordered trees of row IDs) and their changes. A `ForestSpec` names which forest is wanted (a structure, a historical version, a query result, the clipboard, optionally transformed and secured for a user); `ForestService` turns a spec into a `ForestSource`, which gives versioned snapshots, incremental updates and accepts actions.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.a: Actions that a client asks a forest source to perform (add, copy, move, remove rows), their results (applied effects, problems, row ID replacements) and the interaction mechanism by which the plugin asks the caller for a decision before it can complete an action.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: One cell of an export (a header cell or a data cell) as seen by an export renderer. The plugin implements it for each format; renderers call exactly one of the setters to give the cell its value, and the format decides how the value is shown. The same cell object is reused for every row of a column, so a renderer must not keep it after the call returns. Not thread-safe; used only on the exporting thread.

members.setText(String): Sets plain text as the cell value. Null clears the cell (blank in Excel, empty in printable). Printable escapes the text for HTML. Excel truncates text longer than 32767 characters to that length.
members.setNumber(Number): Sets a numeric value. Null clears the cell. Excel stores it as a number (as a double) and applies the column's rounding format if `ExportColumn.setRounding` was called; printable formats it with the user's locale, without grouping separators, and with the column's fixed number of decimals when rounding was set.
members.setPercentage(Double): Sets a percentage given as a fraction (1.0 means 100 %). Null clears the cell. Excel stores the fraction; without a column rounding it is rounded to 4 decimal places of the fraction, with rounding it gets a percent format with that many decimals. Printable shows either a progress bar (value clamped to 0..1) with the percent text, or only the percent text, depending on `PrintableColumn.setPercentageStyle`.
members.setDate(java.util.Date): Sets a calendar date (no time of day). Null clears the cell. The instant is converted to a date in the exporting user's time zone. Excel stores a date value (the renderer should also set `ExcelStyle.DATE` to get date formatting); printable shows the date in the user's date format.
members.setDatetime(java.util.Date): Sets a date with time of day. Null clears the cell. Converted in the exporting user's time zone. Excel stores a date-time value (pair with `ExcelStyle.DATETIME`); printable shows it in the user's complete date-time format.
members.setDuration(Long): Sets a duration in seconds. Null clears the cell. Excel stores it as a fraction of days (seconds / 86400), suitable for the `ExcelStyle.DURATION` hours:minutes format; printable shows it as Jira-style duration text (see `PrintableColumn.setDurationAsCalendarTime`). Durations under one minute in absolute value are shown as zero in printable.
members.setHyperlink(String, String): Sets a link. Arguments: the link text, then the URL. A null URL clears the cell; a null text uses the URL as text. If the URL is not a well-formed absolute URL the cell gets only the text, without a link. Excel creates a URL hyperlink (pair with `ExcelStyle.HYPERLINK` for link look); printable writes an HTML anchor with both parts escaped.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: One column of an export as seen by a renderer while it configures the column. The plugin implements it per format (see `ExcelColumn` and `PrintableColumn`); the renderer receives it in `ExportRenderer.configureColumn`. Settings apply to all data cells of the column. Not thread-safe.

members.getHeaderCell(): Returns the header cell of this column, never null. The renderer normally sets the column title into it with `setText`. In Excel the header cell starts with the left-aligned header style.
members.setRounding(int): Fixes the number of decimal places used for numbers and percentages in this column. The argument is the count of decimals, 0 or more; a negative value throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Printable rounds half-up; Excel applies a number format with that many decimals. Without a call, numbers are shown as given.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: Holder of the well-known keys that the plugin puts into the export context (an `AttributeContext`), so renderers can read export state with `getObject(key)`. The class itself has no behaviour; its nested enums are the keys. These keys are read-only: `putObject` with any of them throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

members.<init>(): Public no-argument constructor with no effect; the class is only a namespace for the nested key enums and is never meant to be instantiated.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: Context keys available only during an Excel export. Each constant is a key for `AttributeContext.getObject`; the value is the current Apache POI object of the workbook being written. They let a renderer do Excel work the API does not cover directly. Values change as the exporter moves through the sheet.

members.POI_WORKBOOK: Key for the Apache POI `Workbook` being written (XSSF for .xlsx or HSSF for .xls). Set once when the workbook is created.
members.POI_HELPER: Key for the workbook's Apache POI `CreationHelper` (for creating rich text, hyperlinks, data formats).
members.POI_SHEET: Key for the Apache POI `Sheet` into which the structure is exported (there is one sheet).
members.POI_ROWNUM: Key for an `Integer`: the zero-based sheet row index of the row currently being written (the header row while columns are configured, then each data row).
members.POI_ROW: Key for the Apache POI `Row` currently being written (header row during column configuration, then each data row).
members.POI_COLUMN: Key for an `Integer`: the zero-based sheet column index of the column currently being configured or rendered.
members.POI_CELL: Key for the Apache POI `Cell` currently being configured (header cell) or rendered (data cell).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: Context keys available in every export format. Each constant is a key for `AttributeContext.getObject`.

members.VIEW_SPECIFICATION: Key for the `ViewSpecification` of the view being exported (the columns and their settings). When the requested view cannot be read, it is a default view with the issue key column and the main (summary) column.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: The export formats the plugin supports. Each has a stable external name used in module descriptors (the format a renderer provider declares) and in export requests.

members.PRINTABLE: The printable HTML page format; external name `printable`.
members.MS_EXCEL: The Microsoft Excel workbook format; external name `ms-excel`.
members.getExternalName(): Returns the stable external name of the format (`printable` or `ms-excel`), never null.
members.forExternalName(String): Returns the format whose external name equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive), or null when none matches, including for a null argument.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: The context given to a renderer while it configures its column and renders cells. It is an `AttributeContext` (user, locale, time zone, base URL, context objects) that also gives access to the attribute values the exporter loaded. Implemented by the plugin; valid only during the export.

members.getValues(): Returns the attribute values loaded for the exported rows, never null (empty when nothing was loaded). Only attributes requested with `ExportRequestContext.requireAttribute` during `prepare` are present. If a column is configured to use the unfiltered forest, the values come from the forest without trailing filter and sort transformations.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: Extension point: renders one column of a view into export cells. Instances come from an `ExportRendererProvider` and are used for a single export. The plugin calls `prepare` once when the export is set up, then `configureColumn` when the header is built, then `renderCell` for each exported row in forest order. If any call throws (including a linkage error), the plugin logs it and ignores this renderer for the rest of the export; other columns are unaffected.

Called once, before the forest and values are loaded. The renderer declares here which attributes it needs (with `requireAttribute`) and may read the forest spec and context objects. If it throws, the renderer is dropped from the export.
members.configureColumn(com.almworks.jira.struct: Called to set up the column: arguments are the column (header cell and column settings) and the render context. The renderer typically sets the header text and format options. Excel calls it once; printable calls it each time the header row is produced, and resets the multiline flag and header cell before each call.
members.renderCell(com.almworks.jira.structure.a: Called for each exported row: arguments are the cell to fill (reused across rows and cleared before each call), the row being exported, and the render context. The renderer sets the cell value, usually from `row.get(attribute)`. For rows the user may not see, `row.get` returns null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: Extension point declared by other plugins (and by the plugin itself) as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` module, optionally restricted to an export format and to a column key. For each exported column the plugin asks the providers in this order: those registered for the column's key and the format, then for the key and any format, then for any key and the format, then for any key and any format; the first non-null renderer wins.

members.getColumnRenderer(com.almworks.jira.stru: Returns a renderer for the given column in the given format, or null if this provider does not handle it (the next provider is then asked). Arguments: the export format, the view column (key and parameters), and the request context. Throwing `StructureProviderException` makes the plugin skip the whole column; any other exception makes the plugin ignore this provider for the rest of the export.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: The context given to renderer providers and to `ExportRenderer.prepare`. It is an `AttributeContext` that also lets a renderer request attribute values to be loaded and tells which forest is exported. Implemented by the plugin.

members.requireAttribute(com.almworks.jira.struc: Asks the exporter to load the given attribute for all exported rows, so it is available later through `ExportRenderContext.getValues` and `ExportRow.get`. Null is ignored. Must be called during `prepare` (or `getColumnRenderer`); later requests have no effect on loaded values.
members.getForestSpec(): Returns the spec of the forest being exported, never null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.E.summary: One row being exported, passed to `ExportRenderer.renderCell`. Implemented by the plugin. Rows come in forest order; the printable format skips the subtrees of collapsed rows, Excel exports all rows. Rows the user may not see are still listed but give no attribute values.

members.getRow(): Returns the full row (item identity, semantics) for this row ID, never null. May throw the row manager's missing-row error if the row no longer exists.
members.getDepth(): Returns the depth of the row in the exported forest: 0 for a top-level row, 1 for its children, and so on.
members.isExpanded(): True if the row was expanded in the client's view at export time; true for every row when the request carried no expand state.
members.isLeaf(): True if the row has no children in the exported forest (it is the last row or the next row is not deeper).
members.get(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attr: Returns the loaded value of the given attribute for this row, or null if it was not loaded, has no value, or the user is not allowed to see the row. The attribute must have been requested with `requireAttribute`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.e.summary: A cell in an Excel export. Extends `ExportCell` with Excel-only settings. Implemented by the plugin; renderers get it by casting the cell when the format is `MS_EXCEL`.

members.setRichTextFromHtml(String): Sets the value from an HTML fragment, converting basic markup to Excel rich text: bold, italic, underline (ins), strike-through (del), subscript, superscript, font colour and monospace runs; a background colour on a panel block becomes the cell background. If the HTML has no visible text but contains an image, the first image that can be loaded is placed in the cell. If the HTML cannot be converted, the raw string is stored as text. Text is truncated to 32767 characters.
members.setStyle(com.almworks.jira.structure.api: Applies one of the predefined cell styles to this cell, replacing its current style. Null means `DEFAULT`.
members.setIndention(int): Sets the indentation level of the cell text, clamped to 0..15. It is reset to 0 before each data cell is rendered and applied after the renderer returns.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.e.summary: A column in an Excel export. Extends `ExportColumn` with the default cell style of the column. Implemented by the plugin.

members.setDefaultStyle(com.almworks.jira.struct: Sets the default style of the whole sheet column. Null means `DEFAULT`. The plugin sets `DEFAULT` before calling `configureColumn`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.e.summary: Predefined Excel cell styles that renderers can apply with `ExcelCell.setStyle` or `ExcelColumn.setDefaultStyle`. Every style aligns content to the top of the cell, except that the header styles align to the bottom.

members.HEADER_LEFT_ALIGNED: Header style: bold, left-aligned, bottom-aligned, thin bottom border. Header cells start with it.
members.HEADER_RIGHT_ALIGNED: Same as `HEADER_LEFT_ALIGNED` but right-aligned, for numeric columns.
members.DURATION: Elapsed time format in hours and minutes, hours not wrapping at 24 (`[h]:mm`); matches durations stored by `setDuration`.
members.HYPERLINK: Link look: dark blue, underlined text.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.p.summary: How a printable column shows percentage values set with `ExportCell.setPercentage`.

members.PROGRESS_BAR: A small progress bar (value clamped to 0..100 %) followed by the percent text. This is also what happens when no style is set.
members.PERCENT_TEXT: Only the percent text, formatted for the user's locale (not clamped).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.p.summary: A cell in a printable (HTML) export. Extends `ExportCell` with raw HTML and CSS classes. Implemented by the plugin; renderers get it by casting the cell when the format is `PRINTABLE`.

members.setHtml(String): Sets the inner HTML of the cell as given, without any escaping or sanitising; null means empty. The caller is responsible for making the HTML safe.
members.addClasses(String[]): Adds CSS class names to the cell's element (`th` or `td`). Each name is HTML-escaped; null or empty names are ignored; duplicates are kept once, in first-added order. Classes are cleared before each new row.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.export.p.summary: A column in a printable (HTML) export. Extends `ExportColumn` with layout and formatting choices. Implemented by the plugin.

members.setMultiline(boolean): When true, data cells may wrap onto several lines; when false (the default, reset before each `configureColumn`), cell content is kept on one line.
members.setPercentageStyle(com.almworks.jira.str: Chooses how percentages are shown in this column. Null (the default) behaves as `PROGRESS_BAR`.
members.setDurationAsCalendarTime(boolean): When true, durations are shown as calendar time (24-hour days, 7-day weeks); when false (default) they use Jira's time-tracking format for the current user, which follows the configured working hours per day and days per week.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Internal extension point for companion apps, declared as a `structure-core-extension` module. The plugin keys each extension by its complete module key. It is asked for extra widget configuration, for extra data to attach to some REST responses, and for its licence information. Every method may return null to contribute nothing.

members.getConfigurationForWidget(): Returns extra configuration for the structure widget in the browser, or null. A non-empty map is included in the widget configuration under the extension's complete module key; null or empty adds nothing.
members.getRestResponseData(Object): Returns extra data to attach to forest, item, poll and effect REST responses, or null for none. The argument is the request data the client sent for this extension (looked up by the extension's complete module key), or null if none was sent. Exceptions are logged and treated as null. A non-null result is added to the response under the module key.
members.getAppSupportInfo(): Returns licence and version information of the companion app for licence listings and the about popup, or null if the app does not report one. The original also used it for its periodic licence reports to the vendor; the replacement sends nothing (SPEC 1.8).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Internal extension point, declared as a `structure-integration-details-provider` module, through which a companion app says which structures it is integrated with, so the structure management pages can show its icon next to them. The plugin labels each provider with its plugin's name.

members.getProductIconUrl(): Returns the URL of the app's icon to show in the structure management pages. If it returns null the provider is skipped when marking structures.
Given a set of structure IDs, returns the subset that this app is integrated with (for example, has its own data on), or null or an empty set for none. Called when listing structures for management; the argument is never null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Internal: describes a companion app for licence displays (and, in the original, for licence reports). Returned by `StructureCoreExtension.getAppSupportInfo`; implemented by companion apps.

members.getLicense(): Returns the app's current licence, never null (`LicenseData.DISABLED` when it has none). Under the replacement's ruling the plugin treats every reported licence as licensed, valid and not expiring.
members.getUserCount(): Returns the number of users the app counts for licensing, or null if unknown.
members.getProductVersion(): Returns the app's version string, or null if unknown.
members.getProductKey(): Returns the app's plugin key, never null; used as the key of the app's entry in licence listings.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Internal component (`app-support-store`, published as an OSGi service) that tells whether a licence serial has been blocked. In the original, serials were blocked as a result of reports to the vendor's server, and a blocked serial made the licence report `REVOKED_LICENSE`.

members.isLicenseBlocked(String): Returns true if the given licence serial is in the blocked list; false for null or an unknown serial. In the replacement nothing is ever reported, so no serial is ever blocked and this always returns false (SPEC 1.8).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: The data model of a licence of the plugin or a companion app: who holds it, its type, limits, dates and validity. Implemented by the licence management code; the constant `DISABLED` stands for no licence. Instances are read-only. Under the replacement's no-Marketplace ruling (SPEC 1.1), the licence the plugin reports for itself and for recognised extensions behaves as licensed, valid and not expiring.

members.DISABLED: Shared instance of `LicenseData.Disabled` with error `NO_ERROR`, meaning 'no licence'.
members.getLicensee(): Returns the name of the licence holder (organisation). `--` when there is no licence.
members.getLicenseType(): Returns the licence type; `DISABLED` when there is no licence. Under the replacement ruling, the effective licence is never `DISABLED`; Not determined: which non-disabled type the replacement reports (the spec only fixes the observable 'licensed' outcome).
members.getSerial(): Returns the licence serial as text (for Marketplace licences, the support entitlement number), or null when there is none.
members.getSerialNumber(): Returns the numeric serial of a vendor-issued licence, or 0 when there is none (always 0 for Marketplace licences).
members.getExpirationTimestamp(): Returns when the licence expires, as milliseconds since the epoch, or 0 if it does not expire. Under the replacement ruling: 0 (no expiry).
members.getMaintenanceExpirationDate(): Returns when maintenance (updates and support) ends, as milliseconds since the epoch, or 0 if not set. Under the replacement ruling: 0.
members.getLicensedServers(): Returns the server IDs the licence is locked to, or null if it is not server-locked.
members.isServerLocked(): True if the licence is valid only on specific servers (`getLicensedServers` is non-null).
members.getMaximumNumberOfUsers(): Returns the user tier of the licence; 0 or less when the licence has no user limit or is absent.
members.isUnlimitedNumberOfUsers(): True if the licence has no user limit. Under the replacement ruling: true.
members.extraChecks(): Performs licence-kind-specific validity checks and throws `LicenseException` with the reason if one fails (for example a revoked or wrong-product licence). Does nothing when all checks pass. Under the replacement ruling it never throws.
members.hasExpiration(): True if the licence has an expiry date. Under the replacement ruling: false.
members.hasMaintenanceExpiration(): True if the licence has a maintenance end date. Under the replacement ruling: false.
members.isMarketplaceLicense(): True if the licence comes from the Atlassian Marketplace rather than from the vendor directly. Under the replacement ruling: false (there is no Marketplace licensing).
members.isValid(): True if the licence is present and passes all checks. Under the replacement ruling: true.
members.getLicenseError(): Returns why the licence is not valid, or `NO_ERROR`; never null. Under the replacement ruling: `NO_ERROR`.
members.isDataCenterCompatible(): True unless the licence hosting is `SERVER`; i.e. legacy and Data Center licences may be used on a Data Center installation. Default implementation derives it from `getLicenseHosting`.
members.getLicenseHosting(): Returns which deployment kind the licence was issued for, never null. The default implementation returns `LEGACY`.
members.getLicenseSource(): Returns where the licence came from, never null. The default implementation returns `MARKETPLACE` when `isMarketplaceLicense` is true and `VENDOR` otherwise.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: The 'no licence' implementation of `LicenseData`: invalid, type `DISABLED`, source `NONE`, with all limits and dates empty, optionally carrying the error that explains why there is no licence. Immutable and thread-safe. `LicenseData.DISABLED` is a shared instance. Under the replacement ruling the plugin never reports itself as unlicensed, but the class remains part of the API.

members.<init>(): Creates a 'no licence' value whose error is `NO_ERROR`.
members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.e: Creates a 'no licence' value that reports the given error from `getLicenseError` (for example why a licence could not be read). Null is accepted and then returned as the error, despite the non-null contract of `getLicenseError`.
members.getLicenseError(): Returns the error given to the constructor (`NO_ERROR` for the no-argument constructor).
members.equals(Object): Equal to another object of exactly the same class carrying the same error.
members.hashCode(): Hash derived from the error only, consistent with `equals`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Checked exception thrown by licence checks (`LicenseData.extraChecks` and the licence manager) to report why a licence is not valid. It carries a `StructureLicenseError`. Under the replacement ruling licence checks never fail, so the plugin does not throw it, but other code may.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.e: Creates the exception with the given error, no message and no cause. The error should not be null (not checked).
Creates the exception with the given error and underlying cause.
members.getError(): Returns the licence error given at construction.
members.toString(): Returns `license error ` followed by the numeric code of the error, for example `license error 1009`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Where a licence came from. Each constant has a stable lower-case key used in REST output.

members.MARKETPLACE: Issued through the Atlassian Marketplace; key `marketplace`.
members.VENDOR: Issued directly by the app's vendor as a signed licence; key `vendor`.
members.BUNDLE: Provided as part of a bundle of another product's licence; key `bundle`.
members.getKey(): Returns the stable lower-case key of the source.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Reasons why a licence is not valid, each with a stable numeric code. Under the replacement ruling the plugin always reports `NO_ERROR` for its own and recognised licences.

members.NO_ERROR: The licence is fine. Numeric code 0.
members.NO_LICENSE: No licence is installed. Numeric code 1000.
members.LICENSE_CERTIFICATE_ERROR: The licence certificate cannot be read or verified. Numeric code 1001.
members.VENDOR_CERTIFICATE_ERROR: The certificate of the issuer that signed the licence is not trusted or cannot be read. Numeric code 1003.
members.NOT_SIGNED: The licence is not signed. Numeric code 1004.
members.NO_METADATA: The licence lacks the required details. Numeric code 1005.
members.INVALID_DATE: A date in the licence is malformed. Numeric code 1006.
members.INVALID_NUMBER: A number in the licence is malformed. Numeric code 1007.
members.BAD_PRODUCT_ID: The licence names a different product ID. Numeric code 1008.
members.EXPIRED: The licence has expired. Numeric code 1009.
members.NO_RELEASE_DATE: The installed app version has no known release date, so maintenance coverage cannot be checked. Numeric code 1010.
members.UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: The installed app version was released after the licence's maintenance ended. Numeric code 1011.
members.UNSUPPORTED_SERVER: The licence is locked to other servers than this one. Numeric code 1012.
members.JIRA_LICENSE_MISMATCH_USERS: The licence's user tier is smaller than the Jira licence's user tier (or Jira is unlimited and the app licence is not). Numeric code 1013.
members.INVALID_PRODUCT: The licence is for a different product. Numeric code 1014.
members.FREE_LICENSE_EXPECTED: A free licence was expected for this installation but another type was found. Numeric code 1015.
members.BAD_CUSTOMER_ID: The customer ID in the licence does not match. Numeric code 1016.
members.REVOKED_LICENSE: The licence serial has been blocked (revoked). Numeric code 1017.
members.TYPE_MISMATCH: The licence type does not fit the installation. Numeric code 1018.
members.UNKNOWN_ERROR: An unexpected error occurred while checking the licence. Numeric code 1019.
members.JIRA_EVAL_LICENSE_MISMATCH: Jira runs on an unlimited evaluation licence while the app licence has a user limit. Numeric code 1020.
members.NO_DATACENTER_SUPPORT: The installation is Data Center but the licence is for Server hosting only. Numeric code 1021.
members.getCode(): Returns the numeric code of the error: 0 for `NO_ERROR`, otherwise a value from 1000 to 1021 (1002 is unused). Codes are stable and appear in messages and REST output.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: The deployment kind a licence was issued for. Each constant has a stable key used in REST output and messages.

members.LEGACY: Older licence with no hosting restriction; usable on Server and Data Center. Key `legacy`. This is what `LicenseData.getLicenseHosting` returns by default.
members.SERVER: Licence for a single-server installation only; not valid on Data Center. Key `server`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.extensio.summary: Kinds of licence. Each constant has a stable lower-case key used in REST output and messages.

members.DISABLED: No licence (or a licence that cannot be used); key `disabled`.
members.DEVELOPER: Licence for developers of add-ons or for development use; key `developer`.
members.FREE: Free licence (for example community or open source); key `free`.
members.DEVENV: Licence for a development or test environment that mirrors a production one; key `devenv`.
members.getKey(): Returns the stable lower-case key of the type.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.F.summary: An immutable description of a folder: its name and, optionally, the structure that owns it. Created through `Folder.named` or `Folder.copy` and a builder; stored and loaded through `FolderManager`. Thread-safe. It does not override `equals` or `hashCode` (identity semantics).

members.getName(): Returns the folder name, never null or blank, with leading and trailing whitespace removed and at most 190 characters long.
members.getOwningStructure(): Returns the ID of the structure the folder belongs to, or null when the folder is not tied to a structure.
members.named(String): Starts a builder for a folder with the given name. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the name is null, empty or only whitespace. A name longer than 190 characters is shortened to 190 characters ending with `...`.
members.copy(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.fol: Starts a builder initialised with the name and owning structure of the given folder. A null argument throws `NullPointerException`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.F.summary: Mutable builder for `Folder`, obtained from `Folder.named` or `Folder.copy`. Each setter returns the same builder. Not thread-safe.

members.setName(String): Replaces the name. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if it is null or blank; names longer than 190 characters are shortened to 190 ending with `...`. Surrounding whitespace is removed when the folder is built.
members.setOwningStructure(Long): Sets the owning structure ID; null means no owner.
members.build(): Creates the immutable `Folder` from the current name and owner. Can be called repeatedly.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.folder.F.summary: Component (OSGi service; also via `StructureComponents.getFolderManager`) that stores folders in the database. Folder IDs are positive integers within the 32-bit range. The manager performs no permission checks; it is the caller's job to check access. Changes are recorded with the item tracker so rows showing the folder refresh. Results are cached. All methods throw `StructureStoppedException` (unchecked) while the plugin is stopped.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.a.summary: Visitor over the four action types, implemented by forest sources and other code that processes actions. Each method may throw `StructureException`, which `ForestAction.accept` passes on.

A request from the plugin for decisions it needs before it can complete an action, carried by `StructureInteractionException`. Each parameter is one question. The caller answers by repeating the same action with each parameter ID set to a chosen value in the parameter map. Immutable.

members.getParameters(): Returns the questions, in order, as an unmodifiable list.

members.getMessage(): Returns the question text to show, in the current user's language.
